title: Chapter 12 — The Eve
description: The night before the election: envelopes moving in the dark, agents who need feeding, and a family that wants you home.

beats.headline: MOVEMENT RESTRICTED FROM MIDNIGHT
beats.text: The police have announced a restriction of movement from midnight till the end of voting. Okada riders are asked to "rest". They are not resting.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Forty polling agents. Each one needs food, water, airtime and ₦5,000, or they sleep at noon and the other side changes the sheets. ₦200,000.

variants.text: You stayed. Good. Now feed the people who stayed with you. Forty agents, ₦5,000 each, food and airtime. ₦200,000.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Agents who don't eat, don't watch.

options.text: Pay half. Promise the rest after.
"Volunteers only. Ask the market women and Tolú's classmates' parents."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: 11 p.m. Seyi comes back with a Ghana-must-go bag. ₦1,000 notes in stacks, with rubber bands.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Tomorrow, at each polling unit, our boys will "thank" voters after they vote. ₦2,000 each. Show the ballot, collect the thank-you. Everybody does it. Owó Ńlá's nephew is doing ₦3,000.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: The bag is open on the table.

options.text: "Take it back to whoever gave it."
Call Ifeoma. Tell her the nephew is doing ₦3,000, and where.

beats.headline: LIVE: CASH AT THE POLLS
beats.text: Our reporter is at three polling units where a candidate's agents are "thanking" voters with ₦3,000. Police are... watching with interest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: 2 a.m. Home. Tolú is asleep on the couch with your old manifesto on her chest. Funke is awake.

variants.text: 2 a.m. Home. The house is quiet the way houses are when someone has left. Tolú is asleep on the couch with your manifesto on her chest.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: Whatever happens tomorrow, come home the same man who left. That's all I ask. (She pulls the blanket over Tolú.) She made a sign. "MY DAD FOR COUNCILLOR (HONEST)". The brackets were her idea.

beats.speaker: tolu
beats.text: (waking up) Daddy? Mummy called. She said to tell you good luck. (She looks at you.) She said it like she meant it. Mostly.

options.text: Sit up with the manifesto. Read it again, every promise.

beats.title: The Eve
beats.summary: Envelopes moved in the dark, or didn't. Your daughter made a sign with brackets. In four hours, the ward decides.
